the numbered-rules engine, swept across every `rules/*` module + `fixes.rs`/`lib.rs`. The first batch pinned two dominant gaps — finding **Locations** (a rule asserted its finding *fired* but never its `target`/`heading`/`field_index`/`data_row` coords, nor the `ri + 1` row arithmetic) and predicate **boundaries** (a proptest suite proved valid values pass but never landed on the exact operator: `<` vs `<=`, `==` vs `!=`). The re-sweep's residuals closed here: the **`fixes.rs` autofix engine** (the DT-vs-numeric label selector 401; `apply_fixes`'s out-of-range bounds guard 855 — a hand-built past-EOL edit the mutant would index into a panic; the risky-fix count + `!include_risky` retain in `fix_document_selective` 981/983; the all-LF Rule-2a negation 149:72; the embedded-LF Rule-6 `'\n'` filter arm 188), **`emit_override_warnings`**'s branch selector (458 + 473×3, killed by a single-facet overlay: LOCA_ID KEY-kept + type-changed ⇒ "overrides" not "demotes", plus type-only and status-only re-declarations), and **`EffectiveDict::fields_with_status`**'s dedup guard (143×3, a file DICT re-declaring the standard KEY heading LOCA_ID). The 7 residuals are all **equivalent** — a total downstream function subsuming a defensive guard: `parse::<usize>` over `!empty && all_digit` (fixes 648, typed_values 72), `and_hms_opt` over the hour/minute range check with the load-bearing `second>60` arm preserved (typed_values 573), `abbr_desc(empty)→None` (groups 133); plus three unreachable-branch cases — `is_nsci`'s `len < n+4` precondition making `i < len` invariant (276), `single_row_group`'s `rows[1..]` already empty at len==1 (284), and `RULE_2A present ⟺ a non-CRLF line exists` (149:36). The 6 timeouts are loop-termination mutants (Rule-7 suffix-search `*=`, `line_format` position `+=`, `consume_run` scan `==`) killed by timeout

the shared emit orchestrator + byte writer. The crate already had solid tests (the whole `arrow_in` transpose, the emit round-trips); the gaps were concentrated in the orchestrator's helpers. Nine new tests close the default-build survivors: **emit.rs** — the Strict error gate (BOTH sides: the `severity == Error` count and `errors > 0`, via a complete clean fixture vs a duplicate-KEY error one — Strict does *not* synthesize the mandatory TRAN/UNIT/TYPE, so the clean fixture carries them); `resolve_meta`'s override-wins-else-fill guard (explicit UNIT wins, blank falls back to the dict); `format_cell` emitting a `DT` **string** verbatim (not through `ags4_str`, which would strip a `T00:00:00`); `collect_units` (PU-typed columns only + non-blank) and `collect_types` (blank + literal-`"TYPE"` exclusion); and `concatenator` (a group's `TRAN_RCON`, else the AGS `"+"`). **error.rs** — `EmitError`'s per-variant `Display` (a whole-`fmt` replacement empties every message). **writer.rs** — the `write_ags4`/`write_ags4_matrix` `i > 0` group separators (one blank BETWEEN groups, none before the first — a single-group test sees neither edge). `arrow_in` is `#[cfg(feature = "arrow")]`, so its 16 mutants are **cfg-false** in the default sweep and were scored honestly with `--features arrow` (12 killed by the existing arm/transpose tests). The 3 residuals are all **equivalent**: the `Utf8`/`LargeUtf8` `cell_value` arms (Arrow's `ArrayFormatter` fallback renders a string identically to the arm's `Value::String`), and `validate()`'s `dict_version` field (`check_parsed` validates with the passed edition-matched `dict` and never reads `opts.dict_version` — it is consumed only by the path-based `check_file`/`fix_document`)

Retro-sweep (laterite#127). **24 of 51 missed on the first pass — a 47% miss rate — and it was one structural hole, not scattered weak assertions: `diff_parsed`, the crate's ONLY public function and the entry point every surface uses (`lat diff`, Python, Node, wasm), had no test at all.** It appeared exactly once in the file: its own definition. The four existing tests all exercised the private helpers *underneath* it (`diff_group`, `changed_cells`), so line coverage looked respectable while the file-level union, the running totals and the include-predicate were never executed by a test. This is the case mutation testing exists for and line coverage structurally cannot see. All 24 classified **real gap** — no inert code, no equivalents. Six new tests: **`diff_parsed`** — the group union across both files (B's order then A-only, reaching the `!b.groups.contains_key` arm), totals summed across groups, an identical group correctly EXCLUDED, and a rows-identical/headings-differ group correctly INCLUDED (the second arm of the predicate — counting rows alone drops a schema-only change). **`diff_group`** — `headings_added` vs `headings_removed` asserted separately (inverting either filter is otherwise silent); the both-sides requirement on KEY headings (an `||` there would build a row key from a heading half the rows lack); and `max_rows_per_group` asserted on BOTH halves — capped rows AND untruncated counts, which the doc comment promises and nothing tested, so a cap that also truncated the counts would have silently under-reported diffs. **A second pass was needed and is the lesson worth keeping:** the first re-sweep still left 6 survivors on the `total_added`/`total_removed` accumulators, because that test's totals were both **0** — and zero is a fixed point of `-=` and `*=` alike. Killing them needed a fixture where the counts are non-zero AND the operands differ: one group netting 1 added + 1 removed (vanishes under `added - removed`) and one netting 2 added + 0 removed (vanishes under `added * removed`), so each wrong operator drops a different group. A count only proves an operator when zero is not the witness.

Retro-sweep (laterite#127), completing the issue's stated scope. 15 missed on the first pass. **The headline is a non-falsifiable assertion in the existing round-trip test**: `bytes_round_trips_with_no_filesystem` asserted `LOCA_NATE == "523145.10"` on a fixture whose input was ALREADY `"523145.10"`, so it passed whether or not the UNIT/TYPE rows survived the sheet — `write_group_row` (which writes only those two rows) could be stubbed to `Ok(())` with every assertion still green. Replaced by a fixture where survival CHANGES the value (`523145.1` + a `2DP` TYPE → `523145.10` only if the TYPE row round-tripped), which kills the stub, the column-shift in that writer, and the reader's `"UNIT"`/`"TYPE"` match arms at once. **`column_width`** was wholly unasserted — replaceable by any constant — despite being documented python-ags4 parity (`min(max(13, max_len+1), 75)`); now pinned at the 13 floor, the 75 ceiling, and an exact value in the unclamped band (the only place `+ 1` is observable), plus a test that the UNIT/TYPE lookup uses the heading's OWN column index. **`format_sf`'s `i < 0` boundary**: at `i == 0` the arms are NOT interchangeable — `{:.0}` rounds half-to-even (matching python-ags4's `f"{v:.0f}"`) while the other arm's `.round()` rounds half away from zero, so 2SF of 12.5 is "12" not "13". **One survivor was nearly misclassified as equivalent and is worth the warning**: `numeric_prefix`'s `prefix.is_empty() || !all_ascii_digits` guard looks redundant with the `parse::<usize>()` that follows, but Rust's integer `FromStr` **accepts a leading `+`** (`"+5".parse::<usize>()` is `Ok(5)`), so dropping the guard turns a malformed `"+5DP"` TYPE into a valid 5-decimal format. Verified with a scratch binary rather than by reasoning. **1 residual, deliberately recorded rather than forced**: `ags4_bytes_to_xlsx_with:164` applies column WIDTHS via `excel_col(i + 1)`; the `* ` mutant shifts every width one column left. calamine exposes no column-width accessor, so asserting it needs a new dev-dependency on a zip reader plus sheet-XML parsing — disproportionate for a display-only property whose *values* are now covered by the `column_width` unit tests. Only the index they land on is unasserted.

**The facade's first sweep** — 23 rows before this one and not one for `laterite`, so phases 4a (`transport.rs`) and 4b (`cert.rs`) landed without this step. Phase 4c of dec-facade-parity. 5 of 48 viable missed on the first pass, all in `fix.rs`, all real gaps in the new tests rather than inert code. **The headline is a non-falsifiable assertion, the same shape 4a's zstd-level test had**: `fixable_rules()` survived being replaced with `vec!["xyzzy"]` because the test round-tripped every advertised label through `only()` — and an unrecognised label simply *selects nothing* and the run succeeds, so a list of nonsense passed exactly as well as the real one. Rewritten to compare the advertised set against the rule labels the fixer actually **emits**, over two fixtures, plus a shape check that each entry is a rule label rather than a word. The other four were the `Repair` record — the ledger a UI puts in front of someone: `label()` asserted only non-empty (now asserted on content), `line()` asserted `None` for the whole-file repair and never that a line-anchored one *has* a line, so hard-wiring `None` satisfied it (now both halves — `pad_short_row` is `Some(5)`, `normalize_crlf` is `None`), and its `Debug` was never rendered. Re-sweep clean: 48 caught, 0 missed. The 33 unviable are the builder methods, whose `self`-returning shape gives the mutator nothing to substitute.

Swept alongside the `fix.rs`/`build.rs` row above, because phases 4a and 4b had landed without a sweep and `mod.rs` is where 4b's real logic lives. 7 missed on the first pass (6 in `mod.rs`, 1 in `cert.rs`). **Two were in code that phase 4c itself introduced**: both non-default arms of the new `validator_kind` helper could be DELETED with the suite green, because the tests that look like they cover them reach the same `ErrorKind` by a different route entirely — `fix`'s missing-file error comes from this crate's own `fs::read`, and a bad `edition("4.9")` is caught by `resolve_edition` before the engine is ever asked. Now reached properly: `validate()` on a missing path for the engine's own `not_found`, and an **AGS3** file for `unsupported_edition`, which is the only way to make the engine emit it. The other five were **four `Debug` impls that could be stubbed out entirely** (`Read`, `Validate`, `Write`, `Certify`) plus `Written::fixes_applied` surviving replacement with `1`. Both are the same failure of assertion shape: `debug_never_prints_the_document` asserted only that the rendering did NOT leak contents, which a `Debug` printing nothing satisfies perfectly, and `> 0` accepts a hard-wired 1. Every case now asserts what the value IS as well as what it is not. Re-sweep clean.

Phase 4d of dec-facade-parity. **22 of 109 viable missed on the first pass — a 20% miss rate — and every one was an accessor whose test compared it against ITSELF.** Four shapes, worth naming because each reads as a real assertion: (1) `Merged::bytes` survived returning an empty slice, because `save` writes `bytes()` and the test compared the file on disk with `bytes()` — both sides move together, so it only proved the accessor agrees with itself; now compared against `text()`. (2) `Revision::winner` survived being replaced with the constant `1`, because the only merge under test had two files and the second won; now a three-file merge asserts the index MOVES to 2. (3) The `GroupChange` counts survived `0`/`1` substitution because the cap test compares a capped run with an uncapped one — a constant satisfies both — and because every fixture happened to remove exactly one row; the fixture now has its own three-borehole baseline so each count is ≥2 or distinct. (4) `keyed`, `headings_removed` and both `line_*` accessors had only ever been exercised on the side that returns the default: a keyed group, an ADDED heading, and no line assertions at all. A custom `ZZZZ` group the dictionary does not know supplies the unkeyed and heading-removed counterparts in one fixture. Two engine behaviours had to be discovered to write the merge tests and are now recorded in them: `X` absorbs a typed column SILENTLY, so an `X`-vs-`2DP` clash widens with no note and only two different non-`X` types (`2DP` vs `3SF`) produce one; and a note's WHERE lives in its `group`/`heading` fields, not in its message text. Re-sweep clean.
